correctness.rationale: For every integer \(q\ge2\), \(d\ge1\), and \(0\le t\le d\), an exact length-\(t\) directed walk is precisely a suffix/prefix match. The all-one event partitions initial bits into \(q^{d-t}\) disjoint blocks of \(q^t\) bits, yielding population \( (2^{q^t}-1)^{q^{d-t}} \); successive differences are the complete first-hitting census. A singleton source proves the sharp time \(d\). Under independent Bernoulli initial bits, the number of empty blocks is binomial. At dimension \(d_h=2^h+h+c\), the mean is exactly \(2^c\) and its block-emptiness probability tends to zero, giving a Poisson limit; adjacent-step means diverge or vanish, proving the two-point law. Two separately implemented programs verified finite full dynamics, exact directed path overlaps, and critical expectations. The all-size assertions follow from these arguments, not those finite computations.

value.rationale: The result determines an entire natural first-hitting-time census for a classical infinite family of word-overlap networks, not an arbitrary graph-size slice. It distinguishes a sharp worst-case \(d\)-step broadcast from an independent-random-data \(\log_q d\)-step clock and gives a nondegenerate Poisson two-point cutoff at \(d=2^h+h+c\). The complete counts and missing-suffix obstruction are natural precision statistics for propagation, beyond the previously established qualitative primitive-graph convergence theorem. No broad arbitrary-graph theorem is claimed.
